fats.narration: 2.2 grams of fat. Saturated fat is only 0.22 grams, an excellent low mark. Polyunsaturated fat is just 0.36 grams, so the beans do not provide much useful fat either. That is not a major problem though. Legumes are supposed to win through slow carbs, fibre, and protein, not fat.

carbs.narration: 59.8 grams of carbs. Starch is 29.9 grams, providing useful staple energy. Fibre is an excellent 15.2 grams, supporting digestion and helping slow the carb response. The glycemic index is only 31, meaning the carbs raise blood glucose relatively slowly. For legumes, this combination of fibre and low glycemic behaviour is one of the main wins.

proteins.narration: 21.6 grams of protein. Essential amino acids score 9 out of 9, meaning all 9 groups the body must obtain from food clear the useful threshold. Bioavailability is 80%, a solid result for bean protein. For legumes, useful protein combined with slow carbs is the whole point, and cannellini beans deliver both.

vitamins.narration: Vitamins barely show up here. Vitamin E is only 1% daily value and vitamin C is 0%. Vitamin C helps the body absorb plant-based iron, so pairing cannellini beans with peppers, lemon, or other vitamin C-rich foods makes nutritional sense. On their own though, the vitamin section is a clear weakness.

minerals.narration: Iron and magnesium are both 37% daily value. Iron supports haemoglobin and oxygen transport, while magnesium supports energy production plus normal nerve and muscle function. Zinc is the softer mark at 25% daily value, but that is still useful for immune function and tissue repair. For legumes, this is a genuinely strong mineral section.

pros.narration: The positives first: creamy texture works in proper meals. They blend into soups and sauces while still holding their shape in salads. Cheap dry pantry staple. A bag stores well and turns into several meals for very little money. Mild flavour takes seasoning well. Herbs, tomato, garlic, and stronger sauces all work.

cons.narration: The cons next: can be rough on digestion. Their fermentable carbohydrates feed gut bacteria, but can also produce gas and bloating. Dry beans take time and planning. Soaking and a full cook make them less convenient than opening a can. They must be cooked properly. Cannellini are white kidney beans, and raw or undercooked beans can retain a natural lectin called P H A. Proper cooking brings it down to safe levels.

closing.summary: Best bits are fibre, a low glycemic index, strong plant protein, and excellent minerals. Weak spots are thin vitamin support, possible digestive discomfort, and dry-bean preparation. Best for steady energy, digestion, and budget meals because fibre supports bowel health, while protein and starch make them a substantial staple. Pair them with vitamin C-rich vegetables to improve iron absorption.
